items.prompt: Calculate the cost-plus selling price per bag for an invented Ondangwa workshop. Total production cost is N$1,800 for 150 bags; the markup is 25% on unit production cost. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Unit cost formula: total production cost ÷ output. Substitution: 1800 ÷ 150 = 12, giving N$12 per bag. Markup: 0.25 × 12 = 3, giving N$3 per bag. Selling price: 12 + 3 = 15, giving N$15 per bag. This is the charge per bag under the pricing rule; it is N$3 above allocated unit production cost and does not establish net profit if other expenses remain.
marking_guidance: Formula: unit cost and selling price relationships, two knowledge marks.
Substitution and working: use the total batch cost, output and stated cost-based markup, two application marks.
Result with currency units: unit cost N$12 and selling price N$15 per bag, two analysis marks.
Interpretation: the price is a charge per bag above the stated unit production cost; other expenses may affect net profit.
